records.title: Espresso
records.description: Espresso is pressure-extracted intensity: 18g in, 36g out, 25-30 seconds. The base of milk drinks.

records.title: Americano
records.description: Americano is espresso lengthened with hot water: clean and strong.

records.title: Cappuccino
records.description: Cappuccino is the classic thirds: dry foam cap, drinkable art.

records.title: Latte
records.description: Latte is the milky canvas: espresso softened under steamed milk.

records.title: Flat white
records.description: Flat white is the Australian intense latte: less foam, more coffee punch.

records.title: Macchiato
records.description: Macchiato is espresso stained with foam: small and strong.

records.title: Cortado
records.description: Cortado is the Spanish equal-parts: no foam, just balance.

records.title: Mocha
records.description: Mocha is dessert coffee: espresso meets chocolate.

records.title: Cold brew
records.description: Cold brew steeps coarse grounds cold for 12-24 hours: smooth, sweet, low acid.

records.title: Iced coffee
records.description: Iced coffee is hot coffee flash-chilled: brew strong over ice.

records.title: Pour over (V60)
records.description: Pour over is the clarity method: spiral pours, paper filter, bright cups.

records.title: Chemex
records.description: Chemex thick filters make the cleanest cup: tea-like and sweet.

records.title: French press
records.description: French press is full immersion: heavy body, simple ritual.

records.title: AeroPress
records.description: AeroPress is the pressure hack: fast, forgiving, endlessly recipe-tweakable.

records.title: Moka pot
records.description: Moka pot is stovetop espresso-ish: strong, nostalgic, Italian mornings.

records.title: Turkish coffee
records.description: Turkish coffee boils powder-fine grounds in a cezve: intense, with grounds settling.

records.title: Espresso grind
records.description: Espresso grind is fine like table salt: too fine chokes, too coarse sours.

records.title: Filter grind
records.description: Drip grind is medium like sand.

records.title: French press grind
records.description: Press grind is coarse like breadcrumbs to avoid sludge.

records.title: Arabica beans
records.description: Arabica is the quality species: sweeter, more acidic, higher grown.

records.title: Robusta beans
records.description: Robusta is the strong species: more caffeine, more crema, harsher.

records.title: Light roast
records.description: Light roast keeps origin character: bright, tea-like.

records.title: Medium roast
records.description: Medium roast balances origin and caramel: the crowd-pleaser.

records.title: Dark roast
records.description: Dark roast is roast flavor forward: smoky, bold, low acid.

records.title: Bean storage
records.description: Store beans airtight, cool, dark — never the freezer for daily use. Buy whole, grind fresh.

records.title: Water for coffee
records.description: Water is 98 percent of coffee: filtered, 90-96 C, not distilled.

records.title: Caffeine content
records.description: Caffeine: espresso shot ~63mg, drip cup ~95mg, cold brew ~200mg. Light roasts edge darker by scoop.

records.title: Latte art basics
records.description: Latte art needs velvet microfoam and a steady pour: start high, finish low and close.

records.title: Dialing in espresso
records.description: Dial in: fix dose, adjust grind for 25-30 seconds. Sour means finer; bitter means coarser.

records.title: Decaf process
records.description: Swiss Water decaf uses water, not chemicals, keeping flavor closest to regular.

records.title: What Coffee Roasters Do
records.description: Roasters transform green coffee: profiling roasts, cupping, sourcing, and packaging. They work in roasteries — alchemists of the bean and authors of flavor.

records.title: A Day in the Life
records.description: Roasters roast batches, cup tables, adjust profiles, and bag fresh — in roasteries smelling of caramelizing sugar. The day is craft plus palate; every great roast is a small triumph.

records.title: Training and Education Path
records.description: Roasters learn through courses, apprenticeships, and the roaster's seat. The craft is learned batch by batch; the palate develops with cupping.

records.title: Green Coffee Basics
records.description: Origins, processing, and grading — the raw material. Understanding green is the foundation; great roasts start with great green.

records.title: Roast Science
records.description: Maillard, caramelization, first crack — the chemistry of the roast. Understanding the curve is the foundation; the roaster conducts the chemistry.

records.title: Roasting Equipment
records.description: Drum roasters, sample roasters, and cooling — the roastery's engine. Good equipment makes consistent roast; the roaster is the instrument.

records.title: Key Terms and Jargon
records.description: Roast language: charge, turnaround, first crack, development, Agtron. The vocabulary of the roast — the roaster speaks bean.

records.title: Developing Roast Profiles
records.description: The signature work: crafting curves that express each coffee. Profile development is the roaster's artistry; the profile is the signature.

records.title: Cupping Mastery
records.description: The evaluation ritual: slurping, scoring, and describing. Cupping is the craft's judgment; the cupper's palate decides.

records.title: Sourcing Green Coffee
records.description: Relationships, harvests, and contracts — buying the raw with care. Sourcing is the roaster's foundation; the relationship makes the coffee.

records.title: Blending
records.description: Combining coffees for balance and consistency — the blender's composition. Blending is strategy; the blend is the house style.

records.title: Production Roasting
records.description: The daily craft: repeating profiles with precision across batches. Production is discipline; consistency is the product.

records.title: Packaging and Freshness
records.description: Valves, seals, and roast dates — delivering fresh. Freshness is the promise; the bag protects the roast.

records.title: Ethics and Professional Conduct
records.description: Roaster ethics: honest sourcing, fair trade, and quality integrity. The roaster's integrity is in the cup; every bag is a promise.

records.title: Troubleshooting Roast Defects
records.description: Experts diagnose baked, scorched, and underdeveloped — with curve fixes. Every defect teaches; the master learns batch by batch.

records.title: Advanced: Roast Curve Analysis
records.description: The deep science: rate-of-rise, airflow, and the perfect curve. Analysis is the craft's frontier; the curve reveals all.

records.title: History of Roasting
records.description: From open pans to Probat drums to craft roasteries — roasting shaped coffee. Roasters carry the flame's history.

records.title: The Business of Roasting
records.description: Margins, wholesale, and retail — the business behind the bean. Business acumen sustains the roastery; the books must balance.

records.title: Teaching and Mentoring
records.description: Master roasters teach the next generation — curves, cupping, and craft passed batch to batch. Teaching roast keeps the craft's standards high.

records.title: Career Path and the Roastery
records.description: Roasters advance to head roaster or roastery owner. Owning the roastery is the dream — one's own profiles, one's own beans.
